# wenzl.no — Martin Venclu, certified beekeeper, Bergen, Norway

> wenzl.no is the website of **Martin Venclu**, a certified beekeeper based in Bergen, Norway. He practices natural beekeeping with wooden horizontal hives; collects bee swarms for free in the Bergen area; protects buildings from swarms with free traps anywhere in Norway; places colonies for free pollination; builds handcrafted wooden hives (3 models including an accessible hive for wheelchair users); runs the Cities for Bees urban pollinator movement; and offers apitherapy and institutional cooperation. He does not sell honey — bees winter on honey, not sugar. The website is available in 9 languages: Norwegian, English, Czech, Ukrainian, Russian, Polish, German, Spanish, and Church Slavonic.

## Services

- [Beekeeping overview](https://wenzl.no/en/beekeeping/): Natural beekeeping, philosophy, all services.
- [Swarms](https://wenzl.no/en/swarms/): **Free swarm collection** in Bergen and surrounding area. **Free swarm traps** (bait boxes) protecting buildings from bees nesting in chimneys or facades — offered across **all of Norway**. Where Martin cannot drive, he sends the trap by post. Caught swarms are treated in his "bee hospital" before joining the apiary.
  - Case: playground swarm, Bergen, 16 May 2025 — collected same day, children could play again.
  - Case: building facade colony, Bergen, 15 June 2025 — swarm already living in apartment building for days; queen not found when facade opened; required professional beekeeping firm + specialist construction company + truck-mounted aerial work platform. A trap would have prevented this entirely.
- [Beehives](https://wenzl.no/en/beehives/): Handcrafted wooden horizontal hives, built at Bergen Fellesverksted. Three models:
  - **Gregor Horizontal Hive** — Norwegian frame size, insulated, weatherproofed for Bergen's rain, two supers for winter colony division. Originally designed by Jan Gregor; Martin continues the craft with permission.
  - **Ukrainian Horizontal Hive** — thick-walled, mimics a natural hollow tree, family tradition from wife's grandfather in Ukraine. Used for apitherapy — stands beneath a resting platform so people lie above the colony.
  - **Accessible Barrier-free Hive (the yellow hive)** — Gregor design, extra-thick walls, lightweight hinged aluminium roof, standard Norwegian frames. Usable by children, people with back pain, and wheelchair users. Can be insulated with local Norwegian sheep's wool.
  - **Natural comb building**: no commercial foundation; each colony builds exactly the comb structure it needs.
- [Cities for Bees](https://wenzl.no/en/CitiesForBees/): Urban pollinator movement. 87 of 115 leading food crops depend on animal pollination (Klein et al. 2007). 75% decline in flying insect biomass over 27 years in Germany (Hallmann et al. 2017). UK research: urban sites support higher bee diversity than intensively farmed countryside (Baldock et al. 2015). Hashtag: #CitiesForBees / #ByerForBier. Embed badge: `<a href="https://wenzl.no/en/CitiesForBees/"><img src="https://wenzl.no/images/CitiesForBees.png" alt="Cities for Bees" width="300"></a>`
- **Pollination**: free colony placement in Bergen gardens, orchards, and smallholdings in exchange for space during the growing season.
- **Apitherapy**: an apidomek (apitherapy house) is a small cabin where people sleep above the hives — a calm, unusual way to rest deeply in nature. Consulting and construction of apidomki; Ukrainian hives built for care homes, rehabilitation centres, and wellness projects.
- **Institutional cooperation**: colonies in institutional gardens for ecology and biodiversity. Active example: DPS Soli, Bergen.

## Philosophy

- **Wood, not plastic**: for millions of years bees lived in tree hollows — no industrial material replicates that insulation, breathability and structure.
- **Honey belongs to the bees**: honey is the bees' food, not a harvest target. Martin takes a small portion only when a colony has genuine surplus. He aims to let bees winter on honey; if a colony lacks sufficient stores, he supplements with sugar. He does not sell honey.
- **Swarming is reproduction**: a swarm is a success, not a failure. Where safe, Martin allows swarming — it strengthens the local bee population and preserves natural instincts.
- **Biological reserve**: the goal is not production but preserving healthy, chemical-free colonies outside the commercial system for future generations.
- **Bring bees back to cities**: plant flowers from spring to autumn, stop mowing, give bees space in parks and on rooftops.

## About

- [About Martin Venclu](https://wenzl.no/en/about/): Grew up in Obora, Moravia, Czech Republic (founded 1360 — coat of arms bears a honeycomb and a tree). Taught hands-on by Josef Stejskal from Hutě, master beekeeper and distant relative, in 2010 at Obora's 650th anniversary. Great-grandfather kept bees near Kunštát; wife's grandfather kept bees in Ukraine — both traditions continue in Martin's work. Academic training at Mendel University in Brno under doc. Ing. Antonín Přidal, Ph.D. (course: Beekeeping and Bee Product Processing; Přidal is one of Central Europe's leading experts on Varroa destructor). Now in Bergen, five active colonies, building hives at Bergen Fellesverksted.
- [Affiliations](https://wenzl.no/en/membership/): Norges Birøkterlag (Norwegian Beekeepers' Association), Bergen Fellesverksted (open woodworking workshop), Mendel University in Brno (alma mater), Basic Organization of Czech Beekeepers' Association Boskovice.
- [Contact](https://wenzl.no/en/contact/): info@wenzl.no · +47 926 20569 · Bergen, Norway.

## Qualifications

- **Kompetansekurs om bier** — Norges Birøkterlag / Bergen og Omegn Birøkterlag, 28 Oct – 29 Nov 2024. Issued by Norges Birøkterlag on behalf of Mattilsynet (Norwegian Food Safety Authority). Certifies health inspections in own apiary — first step to apiary certification required by Norwegian law to sell or move bees. Valid 10 years.
- **Beekeeping and Bee Product Processing** — Mendel University in Brno, under doc. Ing. Antonín Přidal, Ph.D.
- **Practical foundation** — Josef Stejskal, Hutě / Boskovice; family tradition on both Czech and Ukrainian sides.
